notes: GitHub-Actions morphology: functions are run: steps, classes are jobs:/job blocks (2 per file with a uses:-carrying job, 1 in the leaf), import = uses:, branch/io/risk live inside run: shell strings (if/else/fi, curl/wget/yum, eval/exec — yaml embeds shell and counts it). state 1 = the env: block; telemetry = ::debug/::warning workflow commands; doc counts EVERY name:/description: line so step names are deliberately absent. Locked 2026-08-31. A.3 (gitgalaxy#2669): main.yml carried BOTH 'name:' and 'description:', and yaml's doc rule matches each independently (^[ \t]*name:[ \t]+.* | ^[ \t]*description:[ \t]+.*), so doc read 2 against a planted 1. Dropped 'description:' and kept 'name:' -- 'name:' is the real GitHub-Actions workflow key, 'description:' belongs to composite actions, so the remaining line is also the idiomatic one. Step names stay deliberately absent for the same reason (every name: line is another doc hit). A.4 (gitgalaxy#2669): args/avg_func_args ledgered as intended morphology — the args rule matches a `with:` block, which binds to `uses:` and never to the corpus's `run:` steps; planting it would add fake edges to the planted main->a->b->c DAG (ledger args-no-parameter-surface-morphology). gitgalaxy#2646/#2647: yaml's ownership and cleanup rules were None (cells n/a). Now wired, with `author:` planted in main.yml and two teardown verbs replacing no-op run: steps in c.yml, so both record their planted values.  keyword-rosetta#33: probe_bypass was half-planted (1 of 2); the no-op run: step became `chmod 777`, so func_start stays at its planted 3. `curl ... | bash` was rejected -- curl is also an io keyword. api (gitgalaxy#2729): one `on:` trigger block per file placed directly above `jobs:` (main `push:`, a/b/c `workflow_dispatch:`; 1 each) -- non-function surface; the reusable-workflow idiom `on: workflow_call:` (the real public surface of a `uses:`-called workflow) is outside the rule's push|pull_request|workflow_dispatch|issues list AND is a class_start alternative, so it is not planted (rule too narrow); the unindented `jobs:` line stops class_start's 10-line `uses:` lookahead from chaining through `on:`; no overlap, api_orphan_credit and every planted count unchanged. gitgalaxy#2732 (PR #2736) gave yaml spec_exposure, planted once on c.yml (# [SPEC-2732] ...) beside the existing debt markers. The shipped rule is comment-anchored (^[ \t]*#), NOT the unanchored generic bracket-tag rule the issue proposed: comment-stream rules also run over the code stream (coding_analysis applies every rule; comment_analysis adds a second pass), and unanchored the rule scores YAML flow sequences -- `needs: [audit, lint]` alone gave spec_exposure=1 on a comment-free workflow. dead_code stays 0 here and is NOT part of this change: yaml has always defined that rule, so its 0 is a pre-existing comparable measurement, not a new n/a-to-0 flip (gitgalaxy#2732 scopes it out explicitly). Paired plant per docs/GATING.md; ledger entry comment-stream-rules-missing-jcl-yaml retires with this. 2026-09-05 (keyword-rosetta#59): safety 1 -> 2 in a.yml. `continue-on-error: false` was the only one; a workflow-level `permissions: contents: read` is the second, screened clean. Ledger batch5-tier2-morphology-shapes. 2026-09-05 (gitgalaxy#2753, keyword-rosetta#59): the A.4 clause above is SUPERSEDED FOR `args` and stands unchanged for `avg_func_args`. #2753 found the rule narrower than the language on two axes: `with:` is the CALL-SITE block, while the surface a workflow DECLARES is `inputs:` (`on: workflow_dispatch:`/`workflow_call:`, or action.yml's top-level `inputs:`), and the old regex consumed the header through its first key as ONE match, so a five-input block read 1. The shipped rule matches every indented mapping key and a `yaml_parameter_block` scope filter keeps only the keys whose immediate parent is a valueless `with:`/`inputs:`/`args:` header. An `inputs:` declaration needs no `uses:` line, so A.4's actual objection -- fake edges in the planted main->a->b->c DAG -- does not apply to it; that objection stays correct for the `with:` plant it was written about. Planted one input per function definition in each file (main 4 = 3 probes + entry, a/b/c 3 each = 13 corpus-wide, exactly SPEC's "13 function definitions ... each probe taking exactly one argument"), named for the probes SPEC assigns to that file, with `required: false` as the only attribute -- `description:` would be a doc hit, and every input NAME was screened against the whole yaml menu. main.yml keeps `push:` as its api trigger and gains a sibling `workflow_dispatch:` to carry its inputs. Measured per file against the #2753 engine build: ONLY `args` moves (0 -> 4/3/3/3) plus `indent_spaces`, which is not a reported metric; api stays 1 per file (the rule matches the `on:` header once, not once per trigger) and class_start stays 2/2/2/1 (the unindented `permissions:`/`jobs:` line still stops class_start's 10-line `uses:` lookahead). `avg_func_args` stays 0.0 and stays ledgered under args-no-parameter-surface-morphology: yaml's function unit is a `run:` step, which has no parameter surface at all -- the workflow does.
